newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai slims cotton, silk industries.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai slims cotton, silk industries.

text.p: A total of 23 firms in Shanghai's cotton textile and silk industries will close or be merged in the second half of 1996, the Business News reported on Tuesday.
Four factories would apply for bankruptcy, 14 would shut down production completely and five would be taken over.

The changes are part of a major restructuring of the cotton textile and silk sectors of Shanghai, two of its traditional industries, to reduce processing of primary raw material and increase manufacture of high-value-added products, it said.
After the restructuring, the number of silk plants will be reduced to nine employing 5,630 people from the current 17 employing 17,713, the newspaper said.

The number of cotton textile plants will fall to 21 employing 42,540 people from the current 38 employing 101,725, it said, but gave no timetable. As part of this restructuring, production facilities are being moved to the western region of Xinjiang, China's biggest cotton-producing area.

In the first half of 1996, 172,000 cotton spindles, including 60,000 from Shanghai, were moved from other parts of China and have started production in Xinjiang. Negotiations to move an additional 450,000 spindles to Xinjiang are under way.
